# Share-telemetry dev setting (on by default)

Child of **Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation** (AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN).

## Goal

Add a persisted `shareTelemetryDev` boolean field (default **on**) to `SettingsRecord`, and
surface it as a dev-only toggle in `SettingsScene`. The setting is inert (ignored) when not in
dev mode.

## User story

As a player/operator in dev mode, I want telemetry collection to be controllable via a game
setting (on by default), so I can opt out of upload without restarting the server.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `SettingsRecord.shareTelemetryDev: boolean` with `DEFAULT_SETTINGS.shareTelemetryDev === true`.
- `loadSettings()` merges partial/legacy stored records so an existing record without the field
  resolves to `true`; corrupt JSON and non-boolean values fall back to `true` (default).
- Round-trip persistence: saving `false` and reloading returns `false`; `resetSettings()` restores
  `true`.
- `SettingsScene` shows a toggle labelled e.g. "Share telemetry with the dev server (dev mode)"
  **only when** `import.meta.env.DEV`; activating it flips and persists the value. In a non-dev
  build the toggle row is absent and the value is inert.
- Scene read/write accessors and the toggle action are covered by the existing SettingsScene test
  patterns (mirror the telemetry-consent toggle).

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `SettingsRecord`/`DEFAULT_SETTINGS` in `src/core/settingsStore.ts`; `loadSettings()`
  already spreads defaults first, add explicit coercion for the new field so a legacy
  `{}`-shape record still resolves to `true`.
- Add a dev-gated toggle row in `src/scenes/SettingsScene.ts` mirroring `toggleTelemetryConsent`
  and the `saveSettings` call site (~line 517).
- Tests in `src/core/settingsStore.test.ts` and the SettingsScene test suite.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/settingsStore.ts`
- `src/core/settingsStore.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/SettingsScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/SettingsScene.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN child F1 (dev gate helper — the setting is inertness-tested against the gate).

## Deliverables

Setting field + default + persistence tests, dev-gated SettingsScene toggle + tests.

# Dev collection-on-by-default in stock dev mode

Child of **Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation** (AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN).

## Goal

A stock `npm run dev` (no special env vars) collects the run's telemetry to the local JSONL
sink whenever the share-telemetry setting is on, and collects nothing when the setting is off
or in a production build.

## User story

As a maintainer, I want any browser playing the dev-mode game to automatically collect its run
telemetry, so the run can be evaluated without a manual export step.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `resolveEffectiveTelemetryConfig()` (with the settings-driven flag wired in) returns
  `recording: true` with sink `jsonl` when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true and
  `shareTelemetryDev` is true, with **no** `VITE_TELEMETRY_*` env vars set.
- In dev with `shareTelemetryDev === false`, recording is disabled — the game neither collects
  nor uploads (parent AC2). **Plan-time decision:** the setting is the controlling gate for dev
  collection; the env-var escape hatch remains available for production (where it still requires
  consent), and this ordering is asserted by tests.
- In a production build (`PROD === true`) behaviour is unchanged: recording still requires
  `VITE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` plus the consent flag; `shareTelemetryDev` is ignored.
- `PlayScene._initTelemetry()` loads the persisted setting and passes the dev-collection flag
  into config resolution, so a fresh dev session records from run start.
- Unit tests cover the (dev/prod) × (on/off) matrix plus production-consent-unchanged regression,
  and the JSONL sink writes under `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl` in the happy-dom test env.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `src/telemetry/config.ts` (and `consent.ts` resolution) with an optional
  `devCollectionEnabled` flag derived from the setting; default `false` so existing callers and
  production envs are unchanged.
- Change the effective recording gate to `DEV ? (setting || existing-resolved-recording) :
  existing-resolved-recording`, keeping the consent path intact — the exact boolean composition is
  pinned by the tests above.
- Update `PlayScene._initTelemetry()` (~line 3872) to `loadSettings()` and pass
  `settings.shareTelemetryDev`.
- Tests in `config.test.ts`, `consent.test.ts` and the PlayScene suite.

**Key Files:**

- `src/telemetry/config.ts`
- `src/telemetry/consent.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
- `src/telemetry/config.test.ts`
- `src/telemetry/consent.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- F1 (dev gate helper) and F2 (setting field) — collection gating composes with both.

## Deliverables

Dev-gated collection-on-by-default + matrix tests; production behaviour provably unchanged.
data.title: Dev collection-on-by-default in stock dev mode

# Game-side uploader fired at run end

Child of **Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation** (AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN).

## Goal

At run end, when dev mode is active and the share-telemetry setting is on, the game POSTs the
local JSONL sink's accumulated telemetry to the same-origin dev server — fire-and-forget, never
blocking or crashing the game.

## User story

As a maintainer, I want every dev-mode run to deliver its recording to the dev server
automatically at run end, with zero manual export.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new game-side module (e.g. `src/telemetry/devUpload.ts`) exports an upload function that:
  - returns a no-op when the dev gate (F1) is false (non-dev or setting off);
  - reads the accumulated `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl` localStorage content;
  - POSTs it same-origin to `POST /api/telemetry/upload` (endpoint name from F5), body
    `text/plain`/`application/x-ndjson` with the settings/env composition asserted in tests;
  - catches **all** errors (network failure, HTTP non-2xx, empty storage) and never throws.
- Storage/fetch are injected seams so tests need no network or real localStorage.
- `PlayScene._finishRun()` flushes the recorder (`await runTelemetry.flush()` — new async bridge
  via `void this.flushAndUploadDevTelemetry()`), then invokes the uploader fire-and-forget;
  the GameOverScene transition still happens regardless of the upload outcome.
- Tests: fires with the sink content when dev+on; no fetch when dev+off or prod; empty storage ⇒
  no request; rejected fetch ⇒ resolves without throwing; non-2xx ⇒ swallowed; the run-end hook
  still transitions to GameOverScene; the sink's localStorage content is left intact after upload
  (parent constraint — assert no clear-after-upload).

- Parent AC (verbatim): **Upload at end of game.** At run end (the existing `_finishRun`/run-end hook), and
## Minimal implementation

- Add `src/telemetry/devUpload.ts` + `devUpload.test.ts` (inject `fetch`, storage reader, gate).
- Reuse `TELEMETRY_JSONL_STORAGE_KEY` from `src/telemetry/sinks.ts`.
- Hook into `PlayScene._finishRun()` (~line 3255) next to `runTelemetry.runEnd()` /
  `emitRunEndedSignal()`, dev-gated.

**Key Files:**

- `src/telemetry/devUpload.ts`
- `src/telemetry/devUpload.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
- `src/telemetry/sinks.ts` (`TELEMETRY_JSONL_STORAGE_KEY`)

## Dependencies

- F1 (gate), F2 (setting), F3 (collection enabled so a payload exists).

## Deliverables

Uploader module + tests; run-end hook; sink-content-integrity assertion.

# Dev-only upload endpoint with validation and storage

Child of **Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation** (AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN).

## Goal

A Vite dev-only middleware accepts the game's upload, validates the body against the existing
recording reader, stores it under `recordings/session-<timestamp>.jsonl`, and rejects malformed
bodies with a 4xx **without writing anything**.

## User story

As a maintainer, I want the dev server to reliably receive, validate and store uploads from any
browser hitting it, following the established `configCsvPlugin` pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` registers `POST /api/telemetry/upload` only for
  `apply: 'serve'` (mirror `configCsvPlugin`); tests assert it is **not** registered for a
  build/production server and that `plugin.apply === 'serve'`.
- A valid body (≥1 schema-valid JSONL record via `parseRecording`/`parseTelemetryJsonl` from
  `scripts/recording.mjs`) ⇒ 2xx JSON confirmation carrying stored path, record count and run
  count.
- Invalid JSONL, zero valid records, or an unsupported schema version ⇒ 4xx **and no file
  written** (assert the recordings dir is untouched).
- The stored file follows the existing `recordings/session-<timestamp>.jsonl` naming
  (mirror `scripts/record-session.mjs`), is collision-safe/timestamped, and `recordings/`
  remains gitignored (no committed fixtures).
- Oversized bodies are rejected (bounded size, e.g. the existing multi-megabyte local sink size)
  with 4xx before parsing/writing.
- The plugin is registered in `vite.config.ts` next to `configCsvPlugin()`.

- Parent AC (verbatim): **Server-side receipt.** The dev server (Vite dev-only middleware, `apply: 'serve'`,
## Minimal implementation

- Add the plugin mirroring `configCsvPlugin.ts` (JSON helpers, `configureServer`/`apply: 'serve'`).
- Reuse `scripts/recording.mjs` `parseRecording` / `parseTelemetryJsonl` semantics for validation
  (no new parser).
- Tests run the middleware behind a real ephemeral HTTP server against a temp dir, following
  `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` (`startServer` harness with `serve`/`build` modes).

**Key Files:**

- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`
- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.test.ts`
- `./vite.config.ts`
- `scripts/recording.mjs` / `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs`
- `scripts/record-session.mjs` (naming reference)

## Dependencies

- F1 (enforcement scan asserts `apply: 'serve'`; gate module is the source of truth).

## Deliverables

Dev-only upload middleware + validation + storage + tests; plugin registered in `vite.config.ts`.
data.title: Dev-only upload endpoint with validation and storage

# Automatic async human evaluation on uploaded recordings

Child of **Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation** (AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN).

## Goal

After a valid recording is stored, the existing human evaluation pipeline runs automatically,
**asynchronously** (spawned child process — plan-time decision resolving the parent's OPEN
QUESTION), producing the human balance report and companions, with start/completion logged. The
existing `npm run record` and `npm run evaluate -- --human` flows continue to work unchanged.

## User story

As a maintainer, I want balance statistics computed automatically from every uploaded dev
recording without blocking the game or the dev server.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On successful storage, the plugin triggers `node scripts/evaluate.mjs --human <file>
  --out <timestamped output dir under eval-output/uploaded/>` as a **spawned child process**
  (decision: avoids Vite SSR contention with the running dev server).
- The upload HTTP response returns immediately — the evaluation runs in the background and never
  blocks the game or the response.
- Child-process failure (non-zero exit, spawn error) is caught and logged, never crashing the
  dev server; remaining queued evaluations continue.
- The evaluation produces `human-balance-report.json` and companions under the output dir via the
  existing `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` `--human` path (reused as-is — no reimplementation).
- The trigger is injectable/spyable for tests: tests assert spawn arguments, non-blocking
  response, and spawn-error logging without executing a real evaluation.
- Regression: existing `npm run record`-produced files still evaluate via the shipped CLI; the
  existing eval test suites (`src/ai/eval/cli.test.ts`, `humanStats.test.ts`) pass unchanged.

- Parent AC (verbatim): **Automatic evaluation.** After a valid recording is stored, the human evaluation
## Minimal implementation

- Extend `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` with an injected `spawnEvaluation` dependency
  (defaults to `child_process.spawn`), run detach/background with output piped to a log.
- Serialise evaluations (or cap concurrency) to avoid unbounded child processes — plan-time
  decision, asserted by a test.
- Log start, exit code and summary line on completion.

**Key Files:**

- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`
- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.test.ts`
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` / `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` (reused, unchanged)
- `src/ai/eval/cli.test.ts` / `src/ai/eval/humanStats.test.ts` (regression)

## Dependencies

- F5 (storage precedes evaluation trigger).

## Deliverables

Async spawn-based evaluation trigger + tests; non-blocking behaviour proven; evaluator reused.
data.title: Automatic async human evaluation on uploads

# Docs: dev-mode auto-upload and automatic evaluation

Child of **Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation** (AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN).

## Goal

Document the dev-mode automatic telemetry upload and automatic evaluation flow so maintainers
understand the setting, the gate, the endpoint, the storage path, the background evaluation and
how to opt out — while making clear production is unaffected.

## User story

As a maintainer, I want to read how the zero-effort dev telemetry flow works and how to find the
generated balance reports.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/TELEMETRY.md` documents: the new `shareTelemetryDev` setting (default on, dev-only
  toggle), the dev-only gate and its production-unreachability, the `POST /api/telemetry/upload`
  endpoint, the `recordings/session-<timestamp>.jsonl` storage path, the automatic background
  human evaluation and its output location, and how to opt out — explicitly stating production
  telemetry/consent behaviour is unchanged.
- `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` documents the new zero-effort dev flow alongside the
  existing `npm run record` flow, and how to locate the uploaded recordings and
  `human-balance-report.json` outputs.
- Existing docs tests / docs assertions (e.g. telemetry and evaluation docs guards) pass and are

# End-to-end acceptance verification (dev run + production build)

Child of **Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation** (AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN).

## Goal

Verify all parent acceptance criteria on a real dev server run and a production build, and gate
the parent's completion on the evidence.

## User story

As a maintainer, I want proof that the whole flow works end-to-end in dev and is unreachable in
production before the parent feature is accepted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Dev happy path:** stock `npm run dev` (no special env vars), play a run to completion;
  confirm a `recordings/session-*.jsonl` file appears, the background evaluation runs and its
  `human-balance-report.json` (+ companions) appear under the eval output dir, and the dev-server
  console logs the evaluation summary.
- **Opt-out path:** with the setting off in dev, confirm **no** new recording file and **no**
  upload request (game neither collects nor uploads).
- **Production check:** `npm run build` passes (incl. `tsc --noEmit`, `vite build` and
  `check-bundle-hygiene`); `vite preview` serves no upload endpoint; the enforcement scan (F1)
  and full project test suite pass via the project test skill.
- Evidence (screenshots/URLs, file listings, log excerpts, test output) is recorded as a comment
  on the parent work item with the final commit hash.

## Minimal implementation

- Manual dev-run + setting-off run + production build verification steps above.
- Run the full suite via the test skill; triage any failures into critical test-failure items
  per the triage policy.
- Record evidence and a completion comment on AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN.

**Key Files:**

- Evidence/logs referencing `recordings/session-*.jsonl`, the eval output dir, `dist/` bundle and test output.

## Dependencies

- F1–F7 (verification is the final slice).

## Deliverables

Verified acceptance evidence; parent ready for `in_review` only after this passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

## Goal

Verify the campaign arena path's three hard guarantees with acceptance tests, so the balance loop (AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715) can trust the richer reports: byte-identical replay, config sensitivity (a `difficulty-curves.csv` edit or upgrade-definition edit measurably shifts the corresponding distributions for the same seeds), and no wall-clock/IO in the pure eval core (parent AC4/AC5/AC7).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A test replays the same seed + config + policy on the campaign path twice and asserts byte-identical records / stable `recordsHash`.
- **AC2:** A test edits a difficulty-curve row (e.g. raises a wave's `targetDifficulty`) and asserts the same seeds produce a measurably different `waveReached`/`levelReached` distribution.
- **AC3:** A test edits an upgrade definition and asserts the same seeds produce a measurably different `upgradesSelected` distribution.
- **AC4:** A guard test asserts the pure eval core (arena/metrics/engine) never imports a wall-clock or I/O module on its campaign path; campaign progression, upgrade-choice emission, single-source-of-truth, config sensitivity and determinism are all covered by unit tests (parent AC7 umbrella).
- **AC5:** All new tests pass headless under Node/vitest and run in the full suite.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` — byte-identical replay + no-wall-clock guard tests
- `src/ai/eval/engine.test.ts` — recordsHash stability and config-sensitivity batch tests
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — edit target difficulty for sensitivity test
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — POWER_UP_CATALOGUE (edit an upgrade definition for sensitivity test)
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — weapon tuning (alternative upgrade-definition edit target)
- **AC6 (parent-AC4 traceability):** Same seed + config + policy ⇒ byte-identical campaign report; `recordsHash` stable; no wall-clock/IO in the pure eval core.
- **AC7 (parent-AC5 traceability):** Editing `difficulty-curves.csv` (e.g. raising a wave’s `targetDifficulty`) and/or an upgrade definition measurably changes the corresponding report distribution for the same seeds, verified by test.

# Per-describe boot reuse in heavy suites

**Goal:** Reduce per-test boot cost in the heaviest suites by booting one game
per `describe` and resetting scene state between tests instead of booting once
per test (parent Desired change 2). This is a *conditional* improvement: it is
adopted only where a correct state-reset helper exists, because reusing a booted
game can leak state and create new flakes (parent Risks).

**Deliverables**

- A measurement of the current per-test boot cost in the heaviest suites
  (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, gym suites,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) — boot count × boot time,
  recorded with load.
- A shared `resetSceneState()`/`rebootIntoScene()` helper (or an existing helper
  reused) for the suites where reuse is safe, plus the per-describe `beforeAll`
  boot with a `beforeEach` reset.
- Migration of the suites where the reset is provably safe; suites without a
  safe reset keep per-test boot (documented, no regression) and rely on C2/C3
  for the win.
- Evidence (2 consecutive full runs + no new flake items) that no state leak was
  introduced; revert any suite that leaks and record why.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/**/*.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` (shared reset/boot helpers)

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** The per-test boot cost of the heavy suites is measured before the
  change (boot count, per-boot time, wall clock) with load recorded on this item.
- **AC2:** Suites that adopt per-describe reuse boot once per `describe` and
  reset state in `beforeEach`; suites without a provably safe reset are listed
  with the reason they keep per-test boot.
- **AC3:** The full suite passes ≥ 2 consecutive runs with no new load-sensitive
  flake work items filed; any suite that leaks state under reuse is reverted and
  the reason recorded.
- **AC4:** The measured saving is recorded on this item; if the saving is
  negligible or the risk materialises, the experiment is recorded as a negative
  result and the per-test-boot status quo is kept (no speculative churn).

**Dependencies:** blocked by deterministic boot default (C2) and the setTimeout
removal (C6) — reuse is only safe once scene state is driven explicitly.
Depends on C3 for per-project measurement.

**Risk:** shared mutable scene state creating new flakes. Mitigation: only reuse
where a reset helper exists, 2-run validation, revert on any leak.

**References:** Parent AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV § Desired change 2, Risks
(shared mutable scene state), AC5.

# Pure scene-capture module: config parsing, validation and timing

The pure, browser-free core of the multi-scene capture feature (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC): parses and validates the scene-list JSON config, derives the watchable gym scene set, builds the per-scene capture plan (including the two 0.25 s fades), and formats the `--json` payload. No server, browser or Playwright imports — fully hermetic and unit-tested, consumed by the capture driver (sibling item). A shared browser-free registry of watchable gym scene keys mirrors the existing `CAPTURE_SCENARIOS` parity pattern (`scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`) so the CLI pre-boot validation and the page-side director agree on the same set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Covers parent AC1.** A JSON config file specifies an ordered, arbitrary-length list of scenes; each entry carries a `target` (gym scene key), a `playMs` duration, a `captureMs` duration, and an optional `label`. The file is parsed and validated **before** any server/browser boots, failing fast with an actionable, non-zero-exit error for a missing/unreadable/malformed file, an unknown or unsupported `target`, an empty scene list, or a non-positive/non-numeric `playMs`/`captureMs` (mirroring the existing `--count` validation style).
- **Watchable target set.** The watchable gym scene set is derived from the discovered gym scenes minus the parameterised `GymFodderEnemies` and `GymLevel`; unknown or unsupported targets are rejected.
- **Scene-plan builder.** A pure builder computes per-scene `{ target, playMs, captureMs, startMs, endMs }`, inserting the two 0.25 s fades (`SCENE_FADE_MS = 250`) between consecutive scenes; exported, side-effect-free, deterministic.
- **JSON payload builder.** A pure builder reports per-scene timings, the total output duration and the output path.
- **Tests green.** The test-first sibling suite (`Tests: scene-capture config, timing and director keys`) passes; `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` declares the exported types.

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` (new)
- `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` (new)
- `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` (sibling test item)
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` (shared browser-free registry parity pattern)
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` (`parseCaptureCount` validation style reference)
- `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts` (discovered gym scene key convention, `Gym<Name>`)

## Minimal Implementation

1. New shared browser-free registry exported from this module: `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` (the discovered non-parameterised gym keys) and `SCENE_FADE_MS = 250`, following the `CAPTURE_SCENARIOS` parity pattern so the CLI and the director read one source of truth.
2. `parseSceneConfig` / `validateSceneConfig`: read + validate the JSON, reusing the `--count` error style; throw a typed error carrying an actionable message and a non-zero exit mapping.
3. Watchable-set validation against the registry; reject unknown/parameterised targets (`GymFodderEnemies`, `GymLevel`).
4. `buildScenePlan(scenes)`: per-scene `startMs`/`endMs` with the two fades between consecutive scenes; total duration.
5. `buildScenesPayload(...)`: the `--json` shape (per-scene timings + total duration + output path).
6. `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` type declarations matching the project's `.d.mts` convention.

## Dependencies

- Test-first sibling item (its tests define the contract).

## Deliverables

- Hermetic config/validation/planning module + types, consumed by the capture driver and the director.

# Multi-scene capture driver: one recorder, fades, single WebM

The orchestrator slice of the multi-scene capture feature (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC): boots one dev server + one browser, drives the in-page director and the page-side fade overlay, records every scene with a single `MediaRecorder`, and writes exactly one WebM plus the `--json` payload. Reuses the existing capture machinery (server boot, mime selection, audio tap, probe, progress) rather than duplicating it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Covers parent AC3.** A single `MediaRecorder` captures the scenes in config order; between consecutive scenes a page-side canvas overlay fades **to** black over 0.25 s then **from** black over 0.25 s before the next scene's play window, and the fade is present in the recorded video (the recorder captures the overlay). The scene count is arbitrary (verified with at least three scenes).
- **Covers parent AC4.** The command writes exactly **one** WebM (`video/webm;codecs=vp9,opus`, falling back per the existing `resolveCaptureMimeType` order) containing all scenes plus their transitions at 960×540 with the game's own SFX, and the result passes the existing non-trivial video+audio probe. The `--json` payload reports per-scene `{ target, playMs, captureMs, startMs, endMs }` timings and the total output duration/file path.
- **Entry point.** `npm run capture:scenes -- --config <file>` is the documented CLI entry point; the config is parsed and validated before any server or browser boots.
- **Reuse.** Reuses the existing pure capture machinery (Vite server boot, headless Chromium, mime selection, audio tap, probe, progress) rather than duplicating it.
- **Fade injection.** Playwright injects the fade overlay and calls the director between scenes; the recorder and page are never reloaded across the batch.

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` (expose/reuse the server-boot, browser, recorder and probe plumbing, or add a `--scenes` mode)
- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` (sibling pure module — config/plan/payload)
- `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` / `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` (siblings)
- `src/core/captureDirector.ts` (sibling director for in-page scene switching)
- `package.json` (`capture:scenes` script)
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` (documented by the docs item)

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add a `--scenes <config>` mode (or a small sibling orchestrator) reusing the `runCaptureSession`-style server/browser boot and recorder/probe plumbing.
2. Before any boot: parse + validate the config via the pure module; map validation errors to a non-zero exit with an actionable message.
3. One page + one `MediaRecorder`: for each scene, start the gym scene via the director, play for `playMs`, record while capturing for `captureMs`; between scenes inject the page-side fade overlay (fade-to-black 250 ms, then fade-from-black 250 ms) so the recorder captures the transition.
4. Stop the recorder, run the existing probe (`isNonTrivialClip` / `evaluateAudioTrack` / `combineClipVerdict`), and write the single WebM to the configured output path (default under the gitignored `capture-output/` tree).
5. Emit the `--json` payload (per-scene timings + total duration + path); progress reporting reuses `formatProgress`.
6. Register `npm run capture:scenes` in `package.json`.

## Dependencies

- Pure config/planning module (sibling).
- Dev-gated director (sibling) for in-page scene switching.
- (Both of those depend on the test-first item.)

## Deliverables

- A working `npm run capture:scenes` producing one multi-scene WebM with fades plus the `--json` payload.

## Failure Signature

- Test name: src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — playable run (AH-0MU7305Z2003NII3) > AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO AC2 — a live asteroid persists across a level transition
- Failing commit: (not available)
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
Tests 1 failed | 6065 passed | 10 expected fail (6076) — full-suite run (test skill --scope full) failed in two consecutive runs; passes when the file runs alone and under artificial host CPU load.
```

- Actual assertion failure (cached full-suite run, `.worklog/cache/c85c9e0325b819469fa8bfe1e7cab170/stderr.txt`):

```
 FAIL  |integration| src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — playable run (AH-0MU7305Z2003NII3) > AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO AC2 — a live asteroid persists across a level transition
AssertionError: expected false to be true // Object.is equality
 ❯ src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:1629:28
    1627|     expect(wm.level).toBe(2);
    1628|     expect(wm.waveNumber).toBe(1);
    1629|     expect(asteroid.alive).toBe(true);
```

The test walks all ten waves of Level 1 (loop over `wm.waveCount`), then
asserts the carried-over asteroid is still alive on Level 2 — the rock was
dead by then, i.e. it was destroyed at some point during the walk.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. The triage template's `pytest -q -r a … -k '…'` command does **not** apply
   to this repo: the suite is Vitest/TypeScript (`|integration|
   src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`), and agent-initiated test runs must go
   through the test skill (`/skill:test`), never ad-hoc `vitest` (AGENTS.md,
   test-execution policy).
2. Reproduce deterministically on pre-fix code: seed the scene RNG in the
   `bootPlayWithAsteroid()` fixture with `createSeededRng(20261020)` — the
   level-transition test then fails on every run at
   `expect(asteroid.alive).toBe(true)` (`PlayScene.test.ts:1629`). Without a
   seed the heading comes from unseeded `Math.random`, so reproduction is
   probabilistic (which is what the two consecutive full-suite failures were —
   two bad rolls, not a timing condition).
3. Re-run the affected scope after the fix: `/skill:test --type full`
   (audit-accepted full-suite evidence) or `/skill:test --scope changed` for a
   faster loop. Single-file runs are not a sanctioned reproduction channel for
   this load-independent flake.
4. Capture full logs and attach to the work item.

## Root Cause (identified)

- `Asteroid` derives its drift heading from the scene RNG when no exact
  velocity is supplied (`src/entities/Asteroid.ts` constructor:
  `angle = this._rng() * Math.PI * 2`).
- `PlayScene.rng` defaults to `Math.random` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:601`),
  and the public spawn seam `spawnAsteroidAt` passes no `vx`/`vy`
  (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:3685–3692`), so every asteroid spawned by the
  persistence fixture `bootPlayWithAsteroid()` had a random heading.
- Whether that rock survived the ten-wave Level 1 walk therefore varied run to
  run: a heading through the player's position (player collision destroys the
  asteroid — the shared enemy-body collision model), through the auto-fire, or
  through a lingering test bullet (`killNonAsteroidEnemies` leaves
  zero-velocity bullets with a 0.75 s lifetime) destroyed it before the level
  transition. Solo runs and the full suite consume different `Math.random`
  streams, so the symptom was "flaky under full-suite parallel load" even
  though load is not the cause.
- Deterministic reproduction confirmed: `setRng(createSeededRng(20261020))`
  reproduces the failure on every run (implement-session comment, 2026-10-20).

Fix (already implemented, currently **uncommitted** in the parent worktree
`wl-AH-0MVF6VZG9000AN6E-per-describe-boot-reuse-in-heavy-suites`): the fixture
seeds the scene RNG with a fixed seed (`createSeededRng(1)` — heading keeps
the rock clear of the player while retaining both x and y motion so the
"carried-over asteroid continues moving" assertions still hold) and stops the
live rAF loop (`game.loop.stop()`) so an unpredictable real frame cannot
advance the tick-driven tests between `await` points. Verified: the asteroid
subset (61 tests) and the full `PlayScene.test.ts` (247 tests) pass twice
consecutively.

## Coordination

This item is a child of AH-0MVF6VZG9000AN6E (Per-describe boot reuse in heavy
suites); the fixture fix currently sits in that parent's implement worktree
together with the parent's in-flight per-describe changes. AC1 below is
verified once that commit reaches `dev`. If the parent's scope is later
adjusted so the fixture fix no longer ships with it, this item must own the
fix in its own implement worktree (same change, same tests).

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — playable run (AH-0MU7305Z2003NII3) > AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO AC2 — a live asteroid persists across a level transition` passes when run against the latest `dev` (and keeps passing on repeat runs, not just once).
2. All related documentation is updated to reflect the change — at minimum the fixture contract comment in `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (deterministic asteroid fixtures must be seeded / RNG-injected, never `Math.random`-backed). Product docs are unaffected (test-only change).
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes (`/skill:test --type full`).
4. The remediation is deterministic — no `retry`, `skip`, `expected fail`, timeout inflation, or test deletion is used to mask the flake. The persistence fixtures seed the scene RNG and the tick-driven helpers remain the only way the scene advances between assertions.
5. A deterministic reproduction of the pre-fix failure is recorded (seeded-RNG recipe above) so the regression is reproducible and verifiable.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — `bootPlayWithAsteroid()` fixture (root cause + fix location) and the AC2 level-transition test (~line 1612).
- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` — drift heading drawn from `scene.rng` when `vx`/`vy` are absent.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `spawnAsteroidAt` (RNG pass-through) and the `rng = Math.random` default (line ~601).
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` — `bootScene` / `advanceGame`; the live boot-loop behaviour the fix compensates for (`game.loop.stop()`).
- `src/test/powerUpTestFixtures.ts` — `createSeededRng` helper used by the fix.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available — triage template default; the observed cause is a test-fixture RNG bug, owner: tests/build)
